title: Adjunction for the ind-etale closed lift
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $\overline C$ an ind-etale $A/I$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], regarded as an $A$-algebra through the quotient map. Let $H_A(\overline C)$ and $\epsilon_{\overline C}:H_A(\overline C)\to\overline C$ be the colimit algebra and its specified map of [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift]. For every ind-etale $A$-algebra $D$, put $ID=(\operatorname{im}(I\to D))D$. Then the rule $f\mapsto([d]\mapsto\epsilon_{\overline C}(f(d)))$ induces a bijection
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,H_A(\overline C))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{A/I}(D/ID,\overline C),
$$
natural contravariantly in $D$ and covariantly in $\overline C$. Consequently $H_A$, with the maps of [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], is right adjoint to reduction $D\mapsto D/ID$ between the categories of ind-etale algebras (morphisms are algebra homomorphisms).

proof.text: Write $H=H_A(\overline C)$ and $\epsilon=\epsilon_{\overline C}$. By [lem-exc-closed-lift-filtered] the small indexing category in [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift] is filtered; its objects are etale algebras of finite presentation. Thus its colimit $H$ is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Reduction is base change along $A\to A/I$: the quotient $D/ID$ has the universal property of $(A/I)\otimes_A D$, because algebra maps to an $A/I$-algebra are exactly the $A$-algebra maps killing $ID$. The base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] therefore makes reduction a functor on ind-etale algebras. For any $f:D\to H$, the composite $\epsilon f$ kills $ID$: for $a\in I$ and $d\in D$, its value on $ad$ is the image of $a$ in $\overline C$ times $\epsilon f(d)$, hence zero. The quotient universal property gives the specified map $\beta_{D,\overline C}(f):D/ID\to\overline C$.

proof.text: First assume $D$ is etale of finite presentation. Given $u:D/ID\to\overline C$, let $q:D\to\overline C$ be its composite with the quotient. By [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], $(D,q)$ is an indexing object and its coprojection gives a map $\ell(q):D\to H$ with $\epsilon\ell(q)=q$. In the small presentation model, choose a presentation isomorphism $s:P\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ supplied by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and define $\ell(q)=\iota_{(P,qs)}s^{-1}$. For another presentation $t:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}D$, the compatible isomorphism $t^{-1}s:P\to Q$ is an indexing morphism, so the cocone relation gives $\iota_{(P,qs)}=\iota_{(Q,qt)}t^{-1}s$. Thus the map is independent of the chosen presentation and $\beta(\ell(q))=u$.

proof.text: For uniqueness in the finite-presentation case, suppose $f:D\to H$ satisfies $\beta(f)=u$, equivalently $\epsilon f=q$. By [lem-exc-closed-lift-filtered] the indexing category is small and filtered, and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] says that its algebra colimit is also a colimit of the underlying rings. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] with $R=A$, this diagram, $\Lambda=H$, and $g=fs:P\to H$ for the presentation $s:P\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ of [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. It gives an object $(B,q_B)$ and an $A$-algebra map $h:P\to B$ such that $fs=\iota_{(B,q_B)}h$. Applying $\epsilon$ gives $qs=q_Bh$. Hence $h:(P,qs)\to(B,q_B)$ is a morphism of [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift], and the cocone relation gives $fs=\iota_{(P,qs)}$. Therefore $f=\ell(q)$, proving the finite-presentation bijection.

proof.text: For arbitrary ind-etale $D$, choose a small filtered colimit presentation $D=\varinjlim_a D_a$ with etale finite-presentation terms and coprojections $k_a$ using [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Given $u:D/ID\to\overline C$, put $q(d)=u([d])$ and $q_a=qk_a$. Steps 2 and 3 give the unique lift $\ell_a:D_a\to H$ with $\epsilon\ell_a=q_a$. For every transition $r:D_a\to D_b$, both $\ell_br$ and $\ell_a$ compose with $\epsilon$ to $q_a$, so step 3 gives $\ell_br=\ell_a$. The universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] now gives a unique $\ell:D\to H$ with $\ell k_a=\ell_a$. The maps $\epsilon\ell$ and $q$ agree after every $k_a$, hence are equal by the same universal property, so $\beta(\ell)=u$. Any other lift agrees with $\ell$ after every $k_a$ by step 3, and is therefore equal to $\ell$. This proves the full bijection without assuming that a map out of an arbitrary ind-etale algebra factors through one finite stage.

proof.text: For an $A$-algebra map $r:D'\to D$, the formula on quotient classes gives $\beta_{D',\overline C}(fr)=\beta_{D,\overline C}(f)\overline r$, where $\overline r([d'])=[r(d')]$. For $\phi:\overline C\to\overline C'$, the component formula for $H_A(\phi)$ in [def-exc-ind-etale-closed-lift] gives $\epsilon_{\overline C'}H_A(\phi)\iota_{(B,q)}=\phi q=\phi\epsilon_{\overline C}\iota_{(B,q)}$. The universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $\epsilon_{\overline C'}H_A(\phi)=\phi\epsilon_{\overline C}$, and consequently $\beta_{D,\overline C'}(H_A(\phi)f)=\phi\beta_{D,\overline C}(f)$. The same component formula gives $H_A(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $H_A(\psi\phi)=H_A(\psi)H_A(\phi)$ by equality on all coprojections. Thus $H_A$ is a functor and the bijections are natural in both variables; their inverses are natural too by uniqueness in step 4.

source.place: Tag 097P, lemma-lift-ind-etale, proof: Hom equality and final adjunction paragraphs; uniqueness expanded using Algebra Tags 00QO and 07C3

proof.text: An adjunction between these categories means a natural family of bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{A/I}(D/ID,\overline C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,H_A(\overline C))$. The inverses of the bijections proved above give exactly this family, so reduction is left adjoint to $H_A$. Its counit at $\overline C$ is the image of $\mathrm{id}_{H_A(\overline C)}$ under $\beta$, namely $[h]\mapsto\epsilon_{\overline C}(h)$; this is precisely the specified reduction map, an isomorphism by [lem-exc-closed-lift-reduction]. No full-faithfulness theorem is needed for the claimed adjunction.
